_comment: BERC Order 2026/22, published by notification memo 28.01.0000.012.04.003.26.2521 of 3 June
2026. The whole LT-A ladder rose. One day later, Reconsideration Order 2026/01 set aside the
increases to the lifeline and first step only, so slabs 1 and 2 below have a CLOSED knowledge
interval (3-4 June) while slabs 3-7 and the demand charge remain the answer today.
That asymmetry is the point of versioning components rather than schedules: an amended
instrument still governs every row it was not amended in. Resolving June 2026 with no asOf
returns 4.63 from the reconsideration order for the lifeline AND 8.50 from this order for the
second step, in one schedule assembled from two instruments.
Clause 2 of the notification states that existing demand charges are unchanged, which is why
the 42.00 Tk/kW/month rate is re-encoded here at the same value rather than inherited.
Clause 3 names Appendix-kha of this order as fixing the 2026 terms, applicability and
miscellaneous charges, and declares it an inseparable part of the tariff. That appendix is
NOT held. It is the most likely home of the VAT treatment and the prompt-payment rebate, and
both stay UNKNOWN until it is.

components.label: VAT
components.reason: Authoritative calculation rule not yet verified, and the tariff instruments cannot verify it. The 2020 instrument of the same class as the missing 2026 Appendix-kha -- 'Terms, applicability and miscellaneous charges/fees of the Retail Electricity Tariff, 2020', BERC memo 28.01.0000.012.04.003.20.653 of 27 February 2020, clause 2 -- states only that VAT applies on the electricity bill at the rate determined from time to time by the government. The rate and its base are DELEGATED. Gazette S.R.O. 43-Law/2024 likewise states VAT only on its Table-2 service fees, condition (gha). So no tariff order will settle this: the authority is a government/NBR instrument. The universally quoted '5% on energy plus demand' is unsourced here.
components.wouldBeSettledBy: The government/NBR VAT instrument for electricity supply, or an authentic postpaid bill showing the base and its position in the order of operations. NOT BERC Order 2026/22 Appendix-kha, which the 2020 analogue shows would only restate the delegation.

knowledge.basis: Absence established from the notification held; BERC Order 2026/22 Appendix-kha, which the notification names as fixing the miscellaneous charges, is not held

components.label: Prompt-payment rebate
components.reason: No instrument held contains a prompt-payment rebate, and there is positive evidence that the widely quoted '5% for paying within the due date' is an inversion of a real rule pointing the other way: clause 1 of the 2020 terms instrument imposes a 5% one-time LATE-PAYMENT surcharge on all consumer classes, and no rebate appears anywhere in that document. That is a strong hint, not a finding -- absence in the 2020 instrument does not prove absence from the 2026 Appendix-kha, which is not held -- so this stays UNKNOWN rather than being resolved to zero. Note the ONE rebate that is documented is not this one: the 3 June 2026 notification, clause 4, gives PREPAID meter consumers 0.5% on the net bill excluding VAT, and V1 encodes postpaid only.
components.wouldBeSettledBy: BERC Order 2026/22 Appendix-kha, or an authentic postpaid bill. If it turns out there is no prompt-payment rebate, the correct outcome is NOT_APPLICABLE with the surcharge recorded, not a silent zero.
